checkpoints.description: [1/3] per-type rows say 'too few to tell' unless a paired test separates preset and defaults; [2/3] suite v13: thin types (knowledge, long code, long bug fixes, math) to at least 12 and math to 64 so it tunes on 48; [3/3] harder codebase items: fixes from a stack trace or failing test output, and edits that change two functions together

impact_assessment.why: Per-type counts are too small to read, several types have 3-6 questions, and codebase items are single-step
impact_assessment.benefits: Per-type results that can be trusted, a sharper coding signal for complex codebases
impact_assessment.risks: contract: suite v13 makes every profile and the tune:gate baseline stale; state: none; dependency: none; concurrency: the v12 baseline run was stopped
impact_assessment.mitigation: References for every new item pass and plausible wrong answers fail in tests; baseline re-made on v13 after the change

[1/5] stop a sweep's candidate once it cannot catch up, and end the sweep when only the current setting is left; [2/5] pair check: the best two values of the two settings that mattered most, tried together; [3/5] speed on long prompts: the longest code and recall prompts join the speed workload, every prompt weighs the same, first-token time recorded; [4/5] split a task whose fix or format questions are clearly worse under its preset into its own tuned preset, shown in Details; [5/5] use a split preset in chat (needs tune:gate per G-001, ask first)

impact_assessment.why: Tunes take hours, one-at-a-time descent misses interactions, speed ignores long prompts, one preset per task can hurt a question type
impact_assessment.benefits: Shorter tunes with the same decisions, better presets, speed that holds for codebase and long-context use
impact_assessment.risks: contract: profile gains pair, split and long-prompt fields; state: resume markers for the pair check; dependency: none; concurrency: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests per milestone; early stops only drop what provably cannot win; split presets are opt-in until milestone 5

checkpoints.description: [1/5] a value 3+ items behind stops when a rung ends, and the sweep ends with only the current setting left (ADR-062). tests pass, gate 4/4; checklists: passed

[1/3] statistical early stopping: sequential paired McNemar with alpha spending inside each rung, and Holm across surviving challengers for the final change decision; [2/3] discriminating items: aggregate per-item outcomes from stored tune-runs answers, exclude always-right/always-wrong items from the search rungs, keep the full set for final stats/holdout/tune:gate, and record the tuned subset in the profile; [3/3] README, ADRs and gates. The pair check, long-prompt speed and split presets (old [2/5]-[5/5]) are deferred to a later plan

impact_assessment.why: The user asked for honest error control in the tuner and for tuning only on items that can still discriminate for this model; the old gap-3 screen has no error bound and many suite items are saturated per model
impact_assessment.benefits: Fewer false early drops, earlier stops on real evidence, less noise and fewer answers per tune, and a profile that says which items it learned from
impact_assessment.risks: contract: tune options gain looks, sweeps gain pAdjusted/partial, rungs gain final/tunedOn, profiles gain tunedOn; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: sequential stops change some decisions, and the first tune per model still uses the full set because no history exists
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for the sequential stop, the Holm bar, item aggregation and the full-set final stats; the gate keeps using tuneRungs unfiltered; results are compared on the full set

checkpoints.description: [1/3] sequential paired McNemar with alpha spending inside each rung and Holm over surviving challengers for the change decision (ADR-063). tests pass, gate 4/4; checklists: passed

[2/3] per-item outcomes from stored answers, saturated items out of the search rungs, full set kept for final stats/holdout/tune:gate, tunedOn recorded in the profile (ADR-064); [3/3] README and ADRs updated. tests pass, gate 4/4; checklists: passed

[1/5] quiet/battery preset: a measured low-thread preset chosen in Settings; [2/5] portable profiles: export/import a recipe with fingerprint and receipt, warn on mismatch; [3/5] task-aware warnings: surface per-type regressions and measured modes, no type guessing; [4/5] VRAM-fit layer search: try quarter steps instead of max/half; [5/5] model/quant recommender: rank installed and catalog models for this PC

impact_assessment.why: The user wants ModelDuck to be the tool that makes local models efficient per machine, and chose these five product items
impact_assessment.benefits: A quiet laptop mode, profiles that travel, honest type warnings, partial GPU offload that actually fits, and a machine-aware model recommendation
impact_assessment.risks: contract: profiles gain a quiet preset and import/export endpoints, the device stage probes more layer counts, new recommendation route; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: imported profiles can carry another machine's fingerprint
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests per milestone; imported recipes are schema- and range-checked and land as ordinary profiles that warn when stale; the tune gate is unchanged

checkpoints.description: [1/5] Quiet speed preset from the measured threads, Settings Fastest/Light/Quiet (ADR-065); [2/5] portable profile recipes: export/import with validation, receipt and stale warnings, Details buttons (ADR-067). tests pass, gate 4/4; checklists: passed

[3/5] per-type warnings in the overview, Details and chat label, with the preset rate (ADR-068); [4/5] partial GPU offload tries 75/50/25% after a failed full load (ADR-066); [5/5] machine-aware recommendations route and Bench panel, measured first then catalog estimates (ADR-069); README and ADRs updated. tests pass, gate 4/4; checklists: passed

[1/3] type-balanced coding views: write/fix/repo guard so a code preset cannot buy an overall gain by sacrificing a view; [2/3] code-specific prompts and reasoning auto, task-aware prompt axes; [3/3] public code items out of the search, kept in the final check and tune:gate. ADR-070

impact_assessment.why: Coding is the main target: one overall code rate hid regressions on fixes and codebase work, generic prompts missed coding directives, and public items may be memorized
impact_assessment.benefits: A code preset that is good at every coding view, fewer and more relevant prompts, and a search chosen on ModelDuck's own items
impact_assessment.risks: contract: promptAxes gains a task argument, sweeps gain groups/groupGuard; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the code search subset changes and is recorded in tunedOn
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for the view guard and code axes; the guard needs two views of 8+ items; final statistics and the gate still score the whole code task

checkpoints.description: [1/3] code views guard: a candidate clearly worse on write, fix or repo is replaced by one that is not, or the current setting stays; groups and groupGuard are recorded; [2/3] code prompt axes use 8 coding directives and reasoning off/auto/deep, custom lists respected; [3/3] public-code items are excluded from the search rungs and kept in rungs.final and tune:gate (ADR-070). tests pass, gate 4/4; checklists: passed
